method: Manual review of the 100 fixed-seed samples per class from step2-inflection.json. A plural_s/past_ed item is an ERROR if it is not a regular English -s/-es/-ies or -ed/-d/doubled-ed inflection of the classifier's chosen stem (wrong stem, name-only coincidental stem, or base word misread as inflected). A none item is an ERROR if it is clearly a regular -s/-ed form whose stem is in the ascii-first lexicon but the classifier missed it.

errorNotes.manes: stem man; manes is not man+s
errorNotes.hayes: stem hay; Hayes is a name / not hay+s
errorNotes.dais: dais is a base noun, not dai+s
errorNotes.helds: held is past participle, not a plural stem

errorNotes.heed: stem he; heed is a base verb

none.note: No clear false negatives in the 100-sample (no regular -s/-ed with stem present that the classifier omitted). Proper names and loans dominate.

implication: plural_s and past_ed hand-check error rates are 32% and 25% (>10%). Comparator results that depend on those class means must be BOUNDED, not quoted as point figures. The 'neither' class is more reliable (0/100 false negatives in sample); still treat neither-gap as an upper/lower bound pair with contamination from residual false 'neither' and false 'inflected'.
